method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; a seat-neutral core (mai-core.l4, with seven regulative rules for the applicant's and the relevant insurer's duties: ss 59, 60, 65, 66, 102, 154-157, 176), the individual's seat layer (mai-seat.l4) and the relevant insurer's seat layer (mai-seat-insurer.l4), neither restating a rule; mirror cases for the two seats; no REFUSE (a day with no deposited AWE indexed amount, a WPI that is not a whole number, or a work situation with no s 101 start date answers `not covered`, asserted); checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Motor Accident Injuries Act 2019 (A2019-12), Republication No 8, effective 26 December 2025 (last amendment A2025-29), ACT Legislation Register, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/A2019-12.txt; with the Motor Accident Injuries (Indexation of Benefits) Declaration 2026 (No 2), NI2026-402, notified 3 September 2026, amounts on and from 1 October 2026, as deposited at ../../../motor-accident-injuries-indexation-of-benefits-declaration-2026-no-2/registers/source-bundle/NI2026-402.txt, encoded as two dated tables (ss 96, 97, 103: 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027; ss 167, 174, 181: 1 April 2026 to 30 September 2027), the comparison columns used for 1 April to 30 September 2026

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run mai-core.l4 ; l4 run mai-seat.l4 ; l4 run mai-seat-insurer.l4 ; l4 run mai-cases-injured.l4 ; l4 run mai-cases-insurer.l4
checks.result: 270 assertions satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings (2026-10-24); 9 #TRACEs with an expect line (5 breaches by the relevant insurer, 4 obligations pending), each read and as expected; NI2026-402's 30 '1 October 2026' amounts checked against s 18 (1) (c) (earlier figure x factor, rounded up): all agree
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: In: ss 18-19 (AWE indexed amounts, through NI2026-402); s 36 (b); ss 43-50 as facts, with which benefits each limits (ss 89 (3), 112 (2), 132 (2)); s 55; ss 58-59 (application period, late applications, deemed acceptance, the limit); s 60 (1) (receipt notice); s 65 (1)-(4) (liability decision, deemed acceptance); s 66 (1); ss 78-79, 89-92 (income replacement entitlement); s 93, ss 96-98 (the formula, N, SG, the P cap, the workers compensation reduction); s 101 (2)-(5) (period payable); s 102 (fortnightly payment); s 103 (2)-(3) (interim weekly payments); ss 112, 118, 128 (treatment and care: entitlement and period only); ss 132-136, 137 (2) (quality of life entitlement and when to apply); ss 154-157 (which section, the 14-day notice, the reply period, silence); s 167 and table 167; s 239 (1) (the WPI threshold for damages: 'can I sue?' only); ss 168-177 (death benefits: dependant, exclusions, the s 174 amounts, s 175, the earliest s 176 day, the s 177 (2) cap); ss 178-181 (funeral benefits). Out: treatment and care beyond entitlement and period (ss 61-64, 113-127, 129-131); the WPI assessment process (ss 137 (3)-(4), 138-153, 158-166); the significant occupational impact assessment (ch 3); future treatment payments (ch 4); damages amounts (ch 5 beyond s 239 (1)); insurance, premiums and the nominal defendant (ch 6); licensing (ch 7); proof of disentitling offences and the MAI commission declarations (ss 41-50 beyond the facts); dispute resolution (pt 2.10) and ss 67-70; ss 99, 104-107; ss 183-184 except the s 184 (6) route of s 239 (1) (b); pre-injury income (ss 80-88) and its AWE adjustment (s 94), which are inputs. Read with subjects/au/social-security-act-1991 (pension age, compensation recovery), subjects/au/superannuation-guarantee-administration-act-1992 (SG; see finding 20), subjects/au/income-tax-assessment-act-1997 (income replacement benefits as ordinary income) and subjects/au/act/workers-compensation-act-1951 (s 98 reduction, s 50, ss 173, 180); cross-folder IMPORT is not possible.
seats: the person injured in a motor accident (and, after a death, a dependant, the personal representative, or the person who has paid or is liable to pay the funeral expenses)
